title: Acts Chapter 15 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Acts chapter 15 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Acts Chapter 15 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Acts Chapter 15.

questions.question: In Acts 15, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Certain men from Judaea taught the brethren
Paul and Barnabas went to Jerusalem
The church passed through Phenice and Samaria
questions.correctAnswer: Certain men from Judaea taught the brethren
questions.explanation: This event is recorded in Acts 15:1, which states that certain men from Judaea taught the brethren about the necessity of circumcision for salvation.

questions.question: What did Paul and Barnabas determine to do after the dissension?
questions.correctAnswer: Go up to Jerusalem
questions.explanation: Acts 15:2 indicates that Paul and Barnabas determined to go up to Jerusalem to discuss the matter with the apostles and elders.

questions.question: Through which regions did the church pass while declaring the conversion of the Gentiles?
questions.correctAnswer: Phenice and Samaria
questions.explanation: Acts 15:3 mentions that they passed through Phenice and Samaria while declaring the conversion of the Gentiles.

questions.question: How were Paul and Barnabas received when they arrived in Jerusalem?
questions.correctAnswer: With acceptance
questions.explanation: Acts 15:4 states that they were received by the church, apostles, and elders, indicating acceptance.

questions.question: What did certain Pharisees believe was necessary for the Gentiles?
options: To keep the law of Moses
questions.correctAnswer: To keep the law of Moses
questions.explanation: Acts 15:5 reveals that certain Pharisees believed it was necessary to circumcise the Gentiles and command them to keep the law of Moses.

questions.question: What did Peter say God made choice among them to do?
questions.correctAnswer: Preach to the Gentiles
questions.explanation: Acts 15:7 indicates that Peter stated God made choice among them for the Gentiles to hear the word of the gospel.

questions.question: What did God bear witness to regarding the hearts of the Gentiles?
options: He purified their hearts by faith
questions.correctAnswer: He purified their hearts by faith
questions.explanation: Acts 15:9 states that God put no difference between Jews and Gentiles, purifying their hearts by faith.

questions.question: What did Peter question regarding the yoke on the disciples?
questions.correctAnswer: Why tempt God?
questions.explanation: Acts 15:10 shows Peter questioning why they would tempt God by putting a yoke on the disciples that was hard to bear.

questions.question: How does Peter express the means of salvation for both Jews and Gentiles?
options: Through the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ
questions.correctAnswer: Through the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ
questions.explanation: Acts 15:11 states that Peter believes both Jews and Gentiles are saved through the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ.

questions.question: Who spoke after Paul and Barnabas finished declaring their miracles?
questions.correctAnswer: James
questions.explanation: Acts 15:13 states that after Paul and Barnabas had held their peace, James answered and spoke to the brethren.

questions.question: What did Simeon declare about God's visit to the Gentiles?
options: To take out a people for His name
questions.correctAnswer: To take out a people for His name
questions.explanation: Acts 15:14 mentions that Simeon declared how God did visit the Gentiles to take out a people for His name.

questions.question: The Gentiles were declared as having received the Holy Ghost, even as the apostles did.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Acts 15:8 states that God bore witness to the Gentiles, giving them the Holy Ghost just as He did to the apostles.

questions.question: The church did not pass through Samaria during their journey.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Acts 15:3 indicates that the church did pass through Samaria while declaring the conversion of the Gentiles.

questions.question: All Pharisees believed it was unnecessary to circumcise the Gentiles.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Acts 15:5 shows that certain Pharisees believed it was necessary to circumcise the Gentiles.

questions.question: Paul and Barnabas were not received by the church in Jerusalem.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Acts 15:4 states that Paul and Barnabas were received by the church and the apostles in Jerusalem.

medium.title: Acts Chapter 15 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Acts Chapter 15 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did the apostles and elders decide regarding the Gentiles who turned to God?
options: To command them to keep the law
questions.correctAnswer: Not to trouble them
questions.explanation: Acts 15:19 states, 'Wherefore my sentence is, that we trouble not them, which from among the Gentiles are turned to God,' indicating the decision made by the apostles.

questions.question: What does Acts 15:16 promise will happen if someone builds again the tabernacle of David?
options: The residue of men might seek after the Lord
They will receive the Holy Spirit
questions.correctAnswer: The residue of men might seek after the Lord
questions.explanation: Acts 15:17 states, 'That the residue of men might seek after the Lord,' thus indicating the outcome of restoring the tabernacle.

questions.question: What should the Gentiles abstain from according to the letter sent by the apostles?
questions.correctAnswer: All of the above
questions.explanation: Acts 15:20 lists the things they should abstain from: 'But that we write unto them, that they abstain from pollutions of idols, and from fornication, and from things strangled, and from blood.'

questions.question: What does Acts 15:18 imply about God’s knowledge of works?
options: He knows the hearts of men
He is unaware of human actions
All works are known to God from the beginning
questions.correctAnswer: All works are known to God from the beginning
questions.explanation: Acts 15:18 states, 'Known unto God are all his works from the beginning of the world,' indicating God's omniscience.

questions.question: Why did the apostles feel it was good to send chosen men to Antioch?
options: To tell them what to do
questions.correctAnswer: To clarify the gospel
questions.explanation: Acts 15:25 mentions, 'It seemed good unto us, being assembled with one accord, to send chosen men unto you with our beloved Barnabas and Paul,' suggesting the intent to clarify the gospel message.

questions.question: What is the significance of the phrase 'men that have hazarded their lives' in Acts 15:26?
options: They are committed to the Lord's cause
They have failed in their mission
questions.correctAnswer: They are committed to the Lord's cause
questions.explanation: Acts 15:26 states, 'Men that have hazarded their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ,' indicating their dedication to the gospel.

questions.question: According to Acts 15:21, what does Moses represent in every city?
questions.correctAnswer: Those who preach him
questions.explanation: Acts 15:21 notes, 'For Moses of old time hath in every city them that preach him,' highlighting the ongoing teaching of Moses.

questions.question: How did the apostles react to the idea of burdening the Gentiles with the law?
questions.correctAnswer: They opposed it
questions.explanation: Acts 15:10 shows Peter asking, 'Now therefore why tempt ye God, to put a yoke upon the neck of the disciples,' indicating their opposition to burdening the Gentiles.

questions.question: What was the message sent to the Gentiles in Acts 15:23?
options: Greeting from the apostles and elders
questions.correctAnswer: Greeting from the apostles and elders
questions.explanation: Acts 15:23 states, 'The apostles and elders and brethren send greeting unto the brethren which are of the Gentiles,' indicating the purpose of the message.

questions.question: What was the purpose of sending Judas and Silas according to Acts 15:27?
options: To tell the same things by mouth
questions.correctAnswer: To tell the same things by mouth
questions.explanation: Acts 15:27 mentions, 'We have sent therefore Judas and Silas, who shall also tell you the same things by mouth,' emphasizing their role in conveying the message.

questions.question: What does Acts 15:28 suggest about the apostles' decision-making process?
options: It was guided by the Holy Spirit
questions.correctAnswer: It was guided by the Holy Spirit
questions.explanation: Acts 15:28 states, 'For it seemed good to the Holy Ghost, and to us,' indicating that the decision was made with divine guidance.

questions.question: The apostles aimed to avoid burdening the Gentiles. What does this imply about Christian freedom?
options: Christians should follow all the law
Freedom in Christ does not require legalism
Gentiles are not part of the faith
questions.correctAnswer: Freedom in Christ does not require legalism
questions.explanation: The decision not to burden the Gentiles reflects the principle that faith in Christ is not about legalistic adherence to the law.

questions.question: Is it true that the apostles commanded the Gentiles to keep the law of Moses?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Acts 15:24 states that the apostles gave no commandment regarding the law of Moses to the Gentiles, indicating that they did not impose this requirement.

questions.question: Did Peter support the idea of burdening the Gentiles with the law?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Acts 15:10 shows Peter opposing the idea by questioning why they would put a yoke upon the disciples, indicating his support for freedom from the law.

questions.question: Did the apostles send letters to the Gentiles regarding their faith?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Acts 15:23 mentions that the apostles and elders sent letters to the Gentiles, confirming their communication and guidance.

hard.title: Acts Chapter 15 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Acts Chapter 15.

questions.question: According to Acts 15:29, which of the following is NOT one of the things the Gentile believers were instructed to abstain from?
questions.correctAnswer: Circumcision
questions.explanation: Acts 15:29 lists meats offered to idols, blood, things strangled, and fornication as things to abstain from; circumcision is not mentioned in this verse.

questions.question: What was the response of the brethren in Antioch after reading the epistle sent by the apostles and elders in Jerusalem as recorded in Acts 15:31?
questions.correctAnswer: They rejoiced for the consolation
questions.explanation: Acts 15:31 states that when the brethren read the epistle, 'they rejoiced for the consolation.'

questions.question: In Acts 15:32, Judas and Silas were described as prophets. What did they do for the brethren?
options: Preached the gospel to the Gentiles
Exhorted the brethren with many words and confirmed them
questions.correctAnswer: Exhorted the brethren with many words and confirmed them
questions.explanation: Acts 15:32 records that Judas and Silas, being prophets, exhorted the brethren with many words and confirmed them.

questions.question: What happened after Judas and Silas had tarried in Antioch for a time according to Acts 15:33?
options: They were imprisoned by the authorities
They were let go in peace from the brethren unto the apostles
They accompanied Paul on his journeys
questions.correctAnswer: They were let go in peace from the brethren unto the apostles
questions.explanation: Acts 15:33 states that after tarrying there a space, Judas and Silas were let go in peace from the brethren unto the apostles.

questions.question: Who chose to remain in Antioch even after Judas and Silas left, as noted in Acts 15:34?
questions.correctAnswer: Silas
questions.explanation: Acts 15:34 states, 'Notwithstanding it pleased Silas to abide there still.'

questions.question: What caused the sharp contention between Paul and Barnabas as described in Acts 15:39?
options: Disagreement over taking John Mark with them
questions.correctAnswer: Disagreement over taking John Mark with them
questions.explanation: Acts 15:37-39 shows that Barnabas wanted to take John Mark with them, but Paul disagreed because Mark had previously departed from them; this caused the sharp contention.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'ἐξορκίζω' (exorkizō) in Acts 15:28 mean?
questions.correctAnswer: To confirm or establish
questions.explanation: The word 'ἐξορκίζω' in Acts 15:28 is related to confirming or establishing a decision, as the verse speaks of the Holy Ghost and apostles laying no greater burden, confirming the decision.

questions.question: Which literary device is most evident in the structure of Acts 15:1-29, especially in the debate and resolution process?
questions.correctAnswer: Chiasm
questions.explanation: Acts 15:1-29 presents a chiasm structure with the problem (circumcision debate) and resolution (abstaining from certain things) framing the narrative, a common literary device in biblical texts.

questions.question: Which Old Testament prophecy is directly quoted and fulfilled in Acts 15:16-17 regarding the inclusion of Gentiles?
questions.explanation: Acts 15:16-17 quotes Amos 9:11-12, which prophesies the rebuilding of the tabernacle of David and the inclusion of Gentiles, fulfilling the theme of Gentile inclusion in Acts.

questions.question: Which other New Testament passage echoes the decision of Acts 15:29 about abstaining from meats offered to idols?
questions.correctAnswer: 1 Corinthians 8:1-13
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 8 discusses abstaining from eating meat offered to idols to avoid causing others to stumble, echoing the directive in Acts 15:29.

questions.question: What immediately precedes the instruction in Acts 15:29 regarding abstaining from certain things?
options: The apostles and elders sending a letter to Gentile believers
questions.correctAnswer: The apostles and elders sending a letter to Gentile believers
questions.explanation: Acts 15:28 directly precedes 15:29 and describes the apostles and elders deciding to lay no greater burden than these necessary things and sending a letter to Gentile believers.

questions.question: What is the significance of the phrase 'being recommended by the brethren unto the grace of God' in Acts 15:40?
options: It signifies a formal commissioning and prayer for Paul's mission
It indicates Paul was being excommunicated
It suggests Paul was being financially supported
It implies Paul was entering a new religious sect
questions.correctAnswer: It signifies a formal commissioning and prayer for Paul's mission
questions.explanation: Acts 15:40 shows that Paul was commended by the brethren to God's grace, a form of commissioning and prayer for success in his mission.

questions.question: How does the decision in Acts 15:29 reflect the cultural and religious context of the early church?
options: It enforces strict adherence to Mosaic Law on Gentiles
It balances Jewish tradition with Gentile freedom by forbidding only certain practices
questions.correctAnswer: It balances Jewish tradition with Gentile freedom by forbidding only certain practices
questions.explanation: Acts 15:29 shows the early church's effort to respect Jewish sensibilities while not imposing the full Mosaic Law on Gentile converts, forbidding only specific practices considered offensive or immoral.

questions.question: Which Greek term in Acts 15:29 is translated as 'fornication' and what is its broader theological implication in the early Christian context?
questions.correctAnswer: πορνεία (porneia) - sexual immorality
questions.explanation: The Greek word 'πορνεία' (porneia) used in Acts 15:29 broadly refers to sexual immorality, encompassing various illicit sexual behaviors, and was a key ethical concern in early Christian teaching.

questions.question: True or False: According to Acts 15:35, Paul and Barnabas ceased traveling and solely focused on teaching in Antioch after the Jerusalem council.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Acts 15:35 states that Paul and Barnabas continued in Antioch, teaching and preaching the word of the Lord with many others, indicating they focused on ministry there for a time.

theological.title: Acts Chapter 15 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Acts Chapter 15 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Acts 15:11 teach about salvation?
options: Salvation is by grace through faith in Jesus Christ for all, Jew and Gentile alike
Salvation requires strict adherence to the Mosaic Law including circumcision
Salvation is only for the Jewish people as God's chosen nation
Salvation is earned by works and observance of religious rituals
questions.correctAnswer: Salvation is by grace through faith in Jesus Christ for all, Jew and Gentile alike
questions.explanation: Acts 15:11 states, 'But we believe that through the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ we shall be saved, even as they.' This affirms salvation by grace through faith in Christ without distinction of ethnicity or law observance.

questions.question: What doctrine about the role of the Law in the life of believers is taught in Acts 15:10?
options: The Mosaic Law is a burdensome yoke that believers are not able to bear
The Law is a necessary condition for salvation
The Law must be perfectly observed to be acceptable before God
The Law is abolished and irrelevant for all believers
questions.correctAnswer: The Mosaic Law is a burdensome yoke that believers are not able to bear
questions.explanation: Acts 15:10 asks, 'Now therefore why tempt ye God, to put a yoke upon the neck of the disciples, which neither our fathers nor we were able to bear?' indicating the Law's demands are burdensome and not required for salvation.

questions.question: What doctrine about the work of the Holy Spirit among Gentiles is taught in Acts 15:8-9?
options: The Holy Spirit purifies Gentile believers by faith without requiring circumcision
The Holy Spirit only works through Jewish believers who keep the Law
Gentiles must first be circumcised to receive the Holy Spirit
The Holy Spirit selectively works only with the Jewish people
questions.correctAnswer: The Holy Spirit purifies Gentile believers by faith without requiring circumcision
questions.explanation: Acts 15:8-9 describes God giving the Holy Ghost to Gentiles and purifying their hearts by faith, showing the Spirit's work transcends the Law and ethnic boundaries.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Acts 15:18 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Omniscience
questions.explanation: Acts 15:18 says, 'Known unto God are all his works from the beginning of the world,' demonstrating God's attribute of omniscience—His complete and perfect knowledge.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted by God's actions in Acts 15:7-9 regarding the Gentiles?
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty
questions.explanation: In Acts 15:7-9, God sovereignly chooses to grant the Holy Spirit to Gentiles and purify their hearts by faith, showing His sovereign initiative in salvation.

questions.question: How does the Jerusalem Council in Acts 15 prepare for the universal mission of the church seen in later epistles?
options: By affirming salvation by grace and removing the Law's yoke, it opens the gospel to Gentiles without circumcision
By enforcing strict Mosaic Law observance, it limits the gospel to Jews only
By rejecting the Gentiles outright, it restricts mission work to Judea
By emphasizing Jewish exclusivism, it delays Gentile inclusion
questions.correctAnswer: By affirming salvation by grace and removing the Law's yoke, it opens the gospel to Gentiles without circumcision
questions.explanation: Acts 15 resolves the controversy by affirming salvation by grace through faith and not requiring circumcision, thus preparing for the church's global mission in later epistles like Galatians and Romans.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical theme does the reference to the 'tabernacle of David' in Acts 15:16-17 connect to?
options: The restoration of God's kingdom including Gentiles seeking the Lord
The final destruction of the temple and Davidic line
The exclusive salvation of ethnic Israel
The rejection of Old Testament prophecy
questions.correctAnswer: The restoration of God's kingdom including Gentiles seeking the Lord
questions.explanation: Acts 15:16-17 cites prophecy about rebuilding David's fallen tabernacle, symbolizing the restoration of God's kingdom and inclusion of Gentiles, linking to messianic promises in 2 Samuel 7.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Acts 15:20 and Acts 15:29 teach about holiness and community life for Gentile believers?
options: Gentile believers must abstain from idolatry, fornication, eating blood, and strangled animals to maintain fellowship
Gentile believers are free to practice all customs without restriction
Holiness is only required for Jewish believers
Gentile believers must fully observe the Mosaic dietary laws
questions.correctAnswer: Gentile believers must abstain from idolatry, fornication, eating blood, and strangled animals to maintain fellowship
questions.explanation: Acts 15:20 and 29 instruct Gentile converts to abstain from specific practices as essential for holiness and unity in the church, showing a minimal ethical code for fellowship.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about apostolic authority and guidance is taught in Acts 15:22 and Acts 15:28?
options: The apostles and elders, guided by the Holy Spirit, send authoritative letters to Gentile believers
Local churches make independent decisions without apostolic input
The Holy Spirit acts only through personal revelation, ignoring councils
Apostolic authority is irrelevant for Gentile churches
questions.correctAnswer: The apostles and elders, guided by the Holy Spirit, send authoritative letters to Gentile believers
questions.explanation: Acts 15:22 and 28 show the Jerusalem Council, led by apostles and elders and inspired by the Holy Spirit, sending letters to instruct Gentile churches, affirming apostolic authority and Spirit guidance.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about church unity and resolving doctrinal disputes is taught in Acts 15:2 and Acts 15:39?
options: Disputes are addressed through council and separation when necessary, preserving the mission
Disputes must be ignored to maintain superficial unity
Doctrinal differences are unimportant for church mission
questions.correctAnswer: Disputes are addressed through council and separation when necessary, preserving the mission
questions.explanation: Acts 15:2 records the sending of Paul and Barnabas to Jerusalem for resolution, while Acts 15:39 shows their sharp disagreement leading to separation, illustrating biblical ways to handle disputes without fracturing mission.

questions.question: What does Acts 15:1-11 teach that answers the sceptic's claim that Gentile salvation requires circumcision and full Mosaic Law observance?
options: It teaches that salvation is by grace through faith and not by circumcision or Law observance
It mandates circumcision as essential for salvation
It requires Gentiles to become Jews to be saved
It denies the work of the Holy Spirit among Gentiles
questions.correctAnswer: It teaches that salvation is by grace through faith and not by circumcision or Law observance
questions.explanation: Acts 15:1-11 addresses the controversy directly, with Peter and the apostles affirming that God gave the Holy Spirit to Gentiles without circumcision, and salvation is through grace by faith, not Law works.

questions.question: What doctrine about apostolic mission and risk is emphasized in Acts 15:26?
options: Apostles risk their lives for the name of Jesus, demonstrating commitment and authority
Apostles avoid danger and only preach in safe places
Mission is optional and not urgent
questions.correctAnswer: Apostles risk their lives for the name of Jesus, demonstrating commitment and authority
questions.explanation: Acts 15:26 refers to Paul and Barnabas as men who 'have hazarded their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ,' highlighting the costly commitment of apostolic mission.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is reflected in the decision of the apostles and elders in Acts 15:28 regarding the burdens placed on Gentile believers?
questions.correctAnswer: Wisdom
questions.explanation: Acts 15:28 states that it seemed good to the Holy Spirit and the apostles to lay no greater burden on Gentiles than necessary, reflecting God's wisdom in balancing holiness with freedom.

questions.question: What narrative arc connection does Acts 15:36-41 illustrate in the early church's mission history?
options: The expansion of mission through new partnerships and geographical outreach despite internal disagreements
The end of missionary activity after the Jerusalem Council
The failure of the church to spread beyond Judea
The unification of all apostolic efforts under Paul alone
questions.correctAnswer: The expansion of mission through new partnerships and geographical outreach despite internal disagreements
questions.explanation: Acts 15:36-41 shows Paul and Barnabas parting ways but both continuing mission work, illustrating the dynamic and expanding nature of early church missions despite conflicts.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about prophetic ministry and encouragement in the early church is taught in Acts 15:32 and Acts 15:33?
options: Prophets like Judas and Silas both exhorted and confirmed the brethren, strengthening the church
Prophetic ministry was rejected by the early church
Only apostles had authority to teach and confirm
Encouragement was unnecessary once the letter was read
questions.correctAnswer: Prophets like Judas and Silas both exhorted and confirmed the brethren, strengthening the church
questions.explanation: Acts 15:32-33 states that Judas and Silas, as prophets, encouraged the believers with many words and confirmed them, showing the ongoing role of prophecy for edification.
